payload.title: Prepare go-gitutil for its first tagged release
payload.description: Prepare go-gitutil for its first tagged release: adopt gomion's generated workflows, require published dependency versions with no replace, push to GitHub, and propose a version for the owner to tag.
payload.context: go-gitutil holds git helpers extracted from gomion and has never been tagged. Its go.mod requires go-diffutils at the placeholder v0.0.0 and resolves it, go-dt and go-dt/dtx through replace directives pointing at sibling checkouts, so it builds only on this machine. It has no CI or Release workflow, and tags in go-pkgs are created by a repo's generated Release workflow, never by hand. main has one uncommitted go.mod change raising go-dt. The GitHub repo exists with a single LICENSE-only commit that shares no history with the local commits. Decided: require go-diffutils v0.1.0, its latest tag and identical to its current main; a later go-diffutils tag never forces go-gitutil to re-tag, so there is no reason to wait for one.
payload.analysis: 1. Commit the pending go.mod change. 2. Merge GitHub's LICENSE commit with git merge --allow-unrelated-histories origin/main; never force-push. 3. Require go-diffutils v0.1.0 and the latest tags of go-dt and go-dt/dtx, drop every replace directive, and run go mod tidy. 4. Run gomion repo setup to raise go.mod to Go 1.27 and write test.yml and release.yml; gomion repo setup --check must report the repo up to date. Do not hand-edit the generated files. 5. GOWORK=off go build ./... and GOWORK=off go test ./... pass. 6. Push main; create no tags. 7. Propose a first version (v0.1.0 unless something argues otherwise) and a release description, and report them to the owner, who runs the Release workflow. After the push, the first Test run must show zero Actions warnings and notices.

payload.title: Find directory-prefixed tags in Repo.LatestTag
payload.description: Find directory-prefixed tags in Repo.LatestTag so a nested module's latest tag (such as dtx/v0.2.2) is found and compared by its version part.
payload.context: Repo.Tags filters tags by a module's directory prefix but returns them with the prefix still on. Repo.LatestTag then keeps only tags passing semver.IsValid, which rejects every prefixed tag, so for any nested module LatestTag returns ErrNoSemverTags even when tags exist. gomion has the same code in its own copy of this package and tracks the same bug; its fix is meant to come from here.
payload.analysis: In Repo.LatestTag, strip the module's directory prefix before semver.IsValid and semver comparison, and return the full prefixed tag. Add a test with a nested-module fixture holding prefixed tags, plus a root-module case to show root tags are unaffected.

payload.title: Decide what git operations go-gitutil provides for fixtures
payload.description: Decide which git operations go-gitutil provides so test fixtures and gomion can init, add and commit repositories without shelling out themselves
payload.context: Raised by Mike in gomion E-2540 planning on 2026-11-02. gomion's gompkg tests shell out to git directly (init, add, commit with fixed author env) from a test file; gomion also has its own gommod/gitutils package. Mike: git belongs in go-gitutil. Needed first by go-fsfix real repo fixtures and by gomion tests; mocking git is ruled out because it misses edge cases such as permissions.
payload.justification: Mike chose on 2026-11-02 that git behaviour lives in go-gitutil, not in test files; which operations and what shape is his call

fields.context:
Raised by Mike in gomion E-2540 planning on 2026-11-02. gomion's gompkg tests shell out to git directly (init, add, commit with fixed author env) from a test file; gomion also has its own gommod/gitutils package. Mike: git belongs in go-gitutil. Needed first by go-fsfix real repo fixtures and by gomion tests; mocking git is ruled out because it misses edge cases such as permissions.

Scope added from the go-fsfix brainstorm E-2547 (settled with Mike on 2026-11-06; its outcome holds the design). go-fsfix's RepoFixture now always creates a real repository and gains AddClone and AddWorktree, so the fixture operations go-gitutil must offer are: init with a branch name, forced add of every file, commit with a message and ident, clone, and worktree-add on a new branch. Ident is dt.Mailbox (a DisplayName of type dt.EmailDisplayName plus a dt.EmailAddress), which go-dt gains in a task filed from E-2547; go-gitutil defines no identity type of its own and names the field or parameter Ident. The add operation sets advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false so a fixture repo nested in another is recorded as an embedded repository without git's advice message. go-fsfix keeps the *Repo it used and returns it from RepoFixture.Repo(), so init must hand back a usable Repo without a second rev-parse.

payload.title: Reshape Repo with Init, Clone, Add and Commit
payload.description: Reshape go-gitutil onto NewRepo/Open with Init, Clone, Add and Commit methods, one git run function with optional StdIO, package renamed to gitutil, Streamer and StageModuleFiles removed
payload.context: Shape decided in brainstorm E-2548 (read its outcome). Today go-gitutil has no init, no exported clone, no add with --all/--force, and a Commit (Streamer, operations.go) that takes neither ctx nor identity. Git runs three ways: GitRunner.runGit buffered with stderr wrapped (run_git.go), raw exec.Command in OpenRepo with stderr discarded (repo.go), raw streaming exec in Streamer. go-fsfix RepoFixture (E-2568) and gomion tests (E-2559) call the new API; gomion's gommod/gitutils is deleted in E-2556.
payload.analysis:
From E-2548's outcome:
- Rename package gitutils -> gitutil.
- NewRepo(dir, RepoArgs) constructs without I/O; (*Repo).Open(ctx, OpenArgs) replaces OpenRepo (removed, no alias). RepoArgs{StdIO dt.StdIO, Identity}; OpenArgs empty for now.
- Repo methods Init(ctx, InitArgs{Branch, Identity}), Clone(ctx, src, CloneArgs{Local, NoCheckout, Branch, Bare, Identity}), Add(ctx, AddArgs{Paths, Exclude, All, Force}) with Exclude as ':(exclude)<dir>/' pathspecs, Commit(ctx, CommitArgs{Message, Identity, AllowEmpty}). Package-level Open/Init/Clone construct a Repo and call the method.
- Identity: local config at init/clone, GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env at commit; unset means git resolves. Optional strict boolean refuses machine fallback; off by default. No baked-in defaults.
- One run function (ctx, dir, env, stdin, dt.StdIO, args) behind GitRunner, Repo and creation ops; parsed-output ops always capture, human-output ops stream to StdIO when set. Streamer and the package-level Commit/StageModuleFiles/UnstageAll wrappers deleted. StageModuleFiles removed (Go-module knowledge goes to go-goutil); UnstageAll and StageFileContent stay as Repo methods.
- cached_worktree.go uses the exported Clone.
- GitRef and RemoteName move to go-dt's Git-prefixed types once E-2599 lands.

payload.title: go-pkgs package names use singular util
payload.description: Package and repo names in go-pkgs standardize on singular util: gitutil, goutil, diffutil, matching cliutil, logutil, testutil, dnsutil. go-gitutil's package renames from gitutils; go-diffutils renames too. Mike, 2026-11-12 in E-2548: most of ours are singular; standardize on singular, even renaming go-diffutils.

payload.title: Repo follows NewRepo/Open with creation operations as methods and package-level conveniences
payload.description: NewRepo(dir, RepoArgs) constructs without I/O; (*Repo).Open(ctx, OpenArgs) reads state (replacing OpenRepo, removed); Init and Clone are methods on a constructed Repo; package-level Open, Init and Clone construct and delegate so the implementation lives once. Every other method guards against an unopened Repo. Rationale (Mike, E-2548): a NewRepo() always yields a Repo value, which matters for testing and other uses; Repo{} is constructible regardless, so package-level-only constructors never protected against an uninitialized value. Repo also carries an optional dt.StdIO so one type serves both buffered and streaming callers; Streamer is removed. Open rather than Initialize because Init and Initialize on one type is a trap and callers look for Open.

payload.title: Go-module knowledge lives in go-goutil, not go-gitutil
payload.description: go-gitutil offers only git operations (Add with pathspec Exclude, UnstageAll, StageFileContent). Discovering nested go.mod files (FindNestedModules) and any other Go-module logic lives in go-goutil, extracted from gomion's gommod/goutils; callers compose the two. Mike, E-2548: Go module logic should definitely not be in go-gitutil, but instead in go-goutil; go-gitutil should be genericized to support the equivalent functionality.

payload.title: go-gitutil bakes in no fixture defaults; go-fsfix owns identity, branch and commit-message constants
payload.description: go-gitutil's Identity, Branch and Force fields are optional with git's own behaviour when unset, so a production caller gets the machine's git config. The deterministic defaults a test fixture needs (author FSFix Fixture, email fsfix@example.com, message 'Initial commit message (fsfix)', branch main, forced add) are go-fsfix's exported, overridable constants. Mike, E-2548: these seem to be fsfix specific.

payload.title: Create go-gitutil's test module on go-fsfix fixtures
payload.description: Create go-gitutil's test/ module per the tests-live-in-test-modules decision, move diff_parser_test.go into it, and cover Init, Clone, Add, Commit and Open against go-fsfix repo fixtures
payload.context: go-gitutil has no test/ module; its one test, diff_parser_test.go, sits beside the code, which ED-1650 says to move. Brainstorm E-2548 chose to dogfood go-fsfix repo fixtures (E-2568) in go-gitutil's tests; the build-order friction while both change is a go.work tooling concern tracked in gomion E-2561 and endless E-1192, not an architecture one.

fields.outcome:
# Synthesis: what git operations go-gitutil provides for fixtures

Brainstorm with Mike, 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12, with answers relayed from the
gomion (E-2546) and go-fsfix (E-2547/E-2568) sessions. Everything below is
Mike's choice unless marked "proposed" (my proposal he accepted) or "fact".

## The operation set

go-gitutil gains four operations for fixtures and gomion, all on `Repo`:

- `Init(ctx, InitArgs{Branch, Identity})`: `git init -b <branch>`; writes
  `user.name`/`user.email` into the new repo's local config when Identity is set.
- `Clone(ctx, src, CloneArgs{Local, NoCheckout, Branch, Bare, Identity})`:
  exported; cached_worktree.go calls it instead of its private clone. Identity
  is written to the clone's local config, since a clone does not copy the
  source's local config.
- `Add(ctx, AddArgs{Paths, Exclude, All, Force})`: Exclude becomes git pathspec
  magic `:(exclude)<dir>/`, so git filters and no file list is built in Go.
  Force is an ordinary flag, off by default, like git's.
- `Commit(ctx, CommitArgs{Message, Identity, AllowEmpty})`: Identity is passed
  as `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` env for that one process.

Nothing else is new. `RevParse` already reads HEAD. Reset and checkout were
proposed by the E-2568 session for RepoFixture.Reconcile and withdrawn: a
fixture gets clean git state by being recreated (Cleanup then Create), which
measured 41 ms for 10 files and 412 ms for 10,000. Reconcile is disk-only and
never runs git.

## The shape of Repo (Q1, answered via E-2546 and here)

- `NewRepo(dir, RepoArgs) *Repo` constructs with no I/O. Mike: "a NewRepo()
  allows ALWAYS getting a Repo value which can be important for testing or
  other use-cases." He accepts that every other method guards against an
  unopened Repo. His further point: `Repo{}` is always constructible in Go, so
  package-level constructors never protected against an uninitialized value.
- `(*Repo).Open(ctx, OpenArgs) error` does what OpenRepo does today. `Open`,
  not `Initialize`: a type with both `Init` (git init) and `Initialize` (read
  state) is a trap, and people look for Open.
- Package-level `gitutil.Open(ctx, dir, OpenArgs)`, `gitutil.Init(ctx, dir,
  InitArgs)` and `gitutil.Clone(ctx, src, dst, CloneArgs)` each construct a
  Repo and call the method, so the implementation lives once. Both styles are
  offered so callers pick what fits.
- `OpenRepo` is removed, no alias.
- `RepoArgs` holds what describes the Repo for its life: `StdIO dt.StdIO` and
  `Identity`. `OpenArgs` holds what is about the act of opening; empty today,
  kept for evolution.

## Identity (Q2)

- Identity is optional on `RepoArgs`, `InitArgs`, `CloneArgs` and
  `CommitArgs`. Set, it is applied (local config at init/clone, env at
  commit). Unset, go-gitutil passes nothing and git resolves it itself (env,
  repo config, global config, then git's own "Please tell me who you are"
  error). go-gitutil does not pre-check for a missing identity: that would
  refuse on every machine whose identity lives in the user-level git config.
- A strict mode that refuses to fall back to the machine's config is an
  opt-in boolean on the args, never the default.
- go-gitutil bakes in no fixture defaults. The constants are go-fsfix's
  (Q5 → go-fsfix), exported and overridable per fixture:

  | Value | Default |
  |---|---|
  | Author/committer name | `FSFix Fixture` |
  | Author/committer email | `fsfix@example.com` (proposed) |
  | Initial commit message | `Initial commit message (fsfix)` |
  | Default branch | `main` |
  | Force add | on |

  Default branch is a real gap today: gomion's test leaves it to the
  machine's `init.defaultBranch`. Force is on in fixtures because the threat
  is the developer's global excludes file (`core.excludesFile`): a global
  ignore of `.endless/` would silently drop fixture files on one machine only.

## Streamer, Repo and how git runs (Q3, Q4)

- One type. `Repo` holds state plus the optional `dt.StdIO` from RepoArgs.
  `Streamer` is deleted along with the package-level `Commit`,
  `StageModuleFiles` and `UnstageAll` wrappers, which only buffered Streamer's
  output. Mike: streaming is for future callers, not nobody; both benefits in
  one type.
- The rule: operations whose output the package parses (status, rev-parse,
  log, diff) always capture, regardless of StdIO. Operations whose output is
  for a human (commit, add, push, clone, checkout) write to StdIO when set and
  otherwise buffer and return it.
- One run function behind GitRunner, Repo and the creation operations,
  taking ctx, dir, env, stdin, `dt.StdIO` and args; raw `exec.Command`
  disappears from OpenRepo and Streamer. (Fact: today there are three paths,
  GitRunner.runGit in run_git.go buffered with stderr wrapped, OpenRepo in repo.go raw with stderr discarded,
  Streamer.Commit in operations.go raw streaming with no ctx.)

## Go-module knowledge leaves go-gitutil

`StageModuleFiles` finds nested `go.mod` files and stages around them. Mike:
"Go module logic should definitely not be in go-gitutil, but instead in
go-goutil." So:

- `FindNestedModules` moves to go-goutil. gomion's `gommod/goutils` becomes
  go-pkgs/go-goutil, package `goutil`; that extraction is a
  gomion task of its own (the package also holds AST diff, API compatibility,
  dependency analysis).
- go-gitutil keeps the git-only pieces: `UnstageAll`, `StageFileContent`
  (hash-object + update-index), and the new `Add` with `Exclude`.
- gomion composes: `goutil.FindNestedModules`, then `repo.UnstageAll`, then
  `repo.Add(AddArgs{Paths: ["."], Exclude: nested})`.

## Naming

- The package renames from `gitutils` to `gitutil`. Mike: standardize on
  singular `util` across go-pkgs, including renaming go-diffutils. go-diffutils
  is not an Endless project; Mike files that where he tracks it.
- Git domain types (branch name, revision, object id) live in go-dt's root
  package with a `Git` prefix (`GitRefName`, `GitRevision`, `GitObjectID`),
  filed as E-2599 in go-dt. go-gitutil's `GitRef` and `RemoteName` move to
  those types in its implementation task.

## Tests (Q6)

- go-gitutil gets a `test/` module per ED-1650; today it has none and its one
  test, diff_parser_test.go, sits beside the code.
- The test module dogfoods go-fsfix repo fixtures. The build-order friction
  (go-gitutil's tests need a go-fsfix built against the new API) is a tooling
  problem, not an architecture one. Existing tasks: gomion E-2561 (command
  managing go.work across directories) and endless E-1192 (go.work generation
  as a standalone tool).

## The "decoy" files, explained

The term came from the E-2546 session, not Mike. gomion's repo_setup_test.go
fixture places `go.mod` files at `dtx/testdata/x/go.mod` and
`.endless/worktrees/a/go.mod`, with module paths literally `ignored/testdata`
and `ignored/endless`. They are negative cases: gomion's layout classifier
must not treat them as modules. They must be committed because gomion reads
tracked files only ("An untracked go.mod is invisible to CI, so it is
invisible here too"). Better name: excluded-path go.mod files.

## Follow-ups filed

- E-2600 (go-gitutil): Reshape Repo with Init, Clone, Add and Commit. Cleans up
  E-2548; blocks E-2568, E-2559 and E-2556; relates to E-2599.
- E-2602 (go-gitutil): Create go-gitutil's test module on go-fsfix fixtures.
  Blocked by E-2600 and E-2568.
- E-2601 (gomion): Extract gommod/goutils into go-goutil.
- Decisions ED-1658 (singular util names), ED-1659 (Repo NewRepo/Open shape,
  one type with optional StdIO), ED-1660 (Go-module knowledge in go-goutil),
  ED-1661 (go-fsfix owns fixture defaults).
- Not filed, for Mike: rename go-diffutils (not an Endless project). Revise
  E-2556's description: go-gitutil already has Commit, UnstageAll and
  InfoStore, StageModuleFiles is removed rather than carried over, so its
  remaining work is deleting gomion's copy, switching imports, and rewriting
  the three StageModuleFiles/UnstageAll/Commit call sites onto Repo methods
  plus goutil.FindNestedModules.

payload.reason: Task-level decision (Repo's API shape), not a project decision; recorded in E-2600's analysis and E-2548's outcome
Platitude: separation of concerns, no real alternative; the move is tracked by the go-goutil tasks
Task-level decision (where fixture constants live), not a project decision; recorded in E-2600's analysis and E-2548's outcome
Belongs to gomion, not go-gitutil; refiled there

fields.analysis:
From E-2548's outcome:
- Rename package gitutils -> gitutil.
- NewRepo(dir, RepoArgs) constructs without I/O; (*Repo).Open(ctx, OpenArgs) replaces OpenRepo (removed, no alias). RepoArgs{StdIO dt.StdIO, Identity}; OpenArgs empty for now.
- Repo methods Init(ctx, InitArgs{Branch, Identity}), Clone(ctx, src, CloneArgs{Local, NoCheckout, Branch, Bare, Identity}), Add(ctx, AddArgs{Paths, Exclude, All, Force}) with Exclude as ':(exclude)<dir>/' pathspecs, Commit(ctx, CommitArgs{Message, Identity, AllowEmpty}). Package-level Open/Init/Clone construct a Repo and call the method.
- Identity: local config at init/clone, GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env at commit; unset means git resolves. Optional strict boolean refuses machine fallback; off by default. No baked-in defaults.
- One run function (ctx, dir, env, stdin, dt.StdIO, args) behind GitRunner, Repo and creation ops; parsed-output ops always capture, human-output ops stream to StdIO when set. Streamer and the package-level Commit/StageModuleFiles/UnstageAll wrappers deleted. StageModuleFiles removed (Go-module knowledge goes to go-goutil); UnstageAll and StageFileContent stay as Repo methods.
- cached_worktree.go uses the exported Clone.
- GitRef and RemoteName move to go-dt's Git-prefixed types once E-2599 lands.

# Requirements from go-fsfix (E-2568's plan, relayed 2026-11-12)

go-fsfix never execs git itself, so each of these must be possible through go-gitutil. Items marked NEW go beyond what E-2548 settled and are for Mike to confirm when planning this task.

1. Extra environment for every git process: go-fsfix sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 so the machine's config is ignored. Fits the run function's env parameter; expose it on RepoArgs (per-Repo env) so every operation inherits it.
2. Init on a given branch, typed dt.GitBranchName (E-2599).
3. NEW: set repo-local config keys after init: commit.gpgsign=false, core.hooksPath="" and core.autocrlf=false. Needs a Repo.SetConfig(ctx, key, value) operation, or InitArgs.Config map. Identity-in-local-config (above) is the same mechanism.
4. Forced add of everything with advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false, so a nested repo becomes a gitlink without advice output. Add with All+Force exists; the advice flag is a -c argument or a config key.
5. NEW: Commit with separate author and committer (dt.Mailbox, E-2599) and a fixed author and committer date (time.Time), so commit hashes are deterministic across runs. CommitArgs grows Author, Committer, Date; Identity may become these two Mailboxes.
6. Clone a local repo into a sibling directory and check out a given branch. Clone with Branch exists.
7. Add a linked worktree on a given branch, creating the branch if needed. AddWorktree exists in worktree.go; confirm it takes -b.
8. NEW read-side: current branch (exists), log or commit count, status (exists), HEAD's hash (RevParse exists), a tree entry's mode via ls-tree (to see a gitlink), and repo-local config values via Repo.GetConfig.

No reset or checkout: a fixture gets clean git state by being recreated (41-95 ms for 10-1,000 files on git 2.52).

fields.outcome:
# Synthesis: what git operations go-gitutil provides for fixtures

Brainstorm with Mike, 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12, with answers relayed from the
gomion (E-2546) and go-fsfix (E-2547/E-2568) sessions. Everything below is
Mike's choice unless marked "proposed" (my proposal he accepted) or "fact".

**This outcome is our best current understanding, not a specification.** It
records what we knew and chose on 2026-11-12. Implementation (E-2600, E-2602,
E-2568, E-2559) will learn things this discussion could not, and when it does
the design evolves and this outcome is revised. Treat a deviation discovered
during implementation as information, not as a breach.

## The operation set

go-gitutil gains four operations for fixtures and gomion, all on `Repo`:

- `Init(ctx, InitArgs{Branch, Identity})`: `git init -b <branch>`; writes
  `user.name`/`user.email` into the new repo's local config when Identity is set.
- `Clone(ctx, src, CloneArgs{Local, NoCheckout, Branch, Bare, Identity})`:
  exported; cached_worktree.go calls it instead of its private clone. Identity
  is written to the clone's local config, since a clone does not copy the
  source's local config.
- `Add(ctx, AddArgs{Paths, Exclude, All, Force})`: Exclude becomes git pathspec
  magic `:(exclude)<dir>/`, so git filters and no file list is built in Go.
  Force is an ordinary flag, off by default, like git's.
- `Commit(ctx, CommitArgs{Message, Identity, AllowEmpty})`: Identity is passed
  as `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` env for that one process.

Nothing else is new. `RevParse` already reads HEAD. Reset and checkout were
proposed by the E-2568 session for RepoFixture.Reconcile and withdrawn: a
fixture gets clean git state by being recreated (Cleanup then Create), which
measured 41 ms for 10 files and 412 ms for 10,000. Reconcile is disk-only and
never runs git.

## The shape of Repo (Q1, answered via E-2546 and here)

- `NewRepo(dir, RepoArgs) *Repo` constructs with no I/O. Mike: "a NewRepo()
  allows ALWAYS getting a Repo value which can be important for testing or
  other use-cases." He accepts that every other method guards against an
  unopened Repo. His further point: `Repo{}` is always constructible in Go, so
  package-level constructors never protected against an uninitialized value.
- `(*Repo).Open(ctx, OpenArgs) error` does what OpenRepo does today. `Open`,
  not `Initialize`: a type with both `Init` (git init) and `Initialize` (read
  state) is a trap, and people look for Open.
- Package-level `gitutil.Open(ctx, dir, OpenArgs)`, `gitutil.Init(ctx, dir,
  InitArgs)` and `gitutil.Clone(ctx, src, dst, CloneArgs)` each construct a
  Repo and call the method, so the implementation lives once. Both styles are
  offered so callers pick what fits.
- `OpenRepo` is removed, no alias.
- `RepoArgs` holds what describes the Repo for its life: `StdIO dt.StdIO` and
  `Identity`. `OpenArgs` holds what is about the act of opening; empty today,
  kept for evolution.

## Identity (Q2)

- Identity is optional on `RepoArgs`, `InitArgs`, `CloneArgs` and
  `CommitArgs`. Set, it is applied (local config at init/clone, env at
  commit). Unset, go-gitutil passes nothing and git resolves it itself (env,
  repo config, global config, then git's own "Please tell me who you are"
  error). go-gitutil does not pre-check for a missing identity: that would
  refuse on every machine whose identity lives in the user-level git config.
- A strict mode that refuses to fall back to the machine's config is an
  opt-in boolean on the args, never the default.
- go-gitutil bakes in no fixture defaults. The constants are go-fsfix's
  (Q5 → go-fsfix), exported and overridable per fixture:

  | Value | Default |
  |---|---|
  | Author/committer name | `FSFix Fixture` |
  | Author/committer email | `fsfix@example.com` (proposed) |
  | Initial commit message | `Initial commit message (fsfix)` |
  | Default branch | `main` |
  | Force add | on |

  Default branch is a real gap today: gomion's test leaves it to the
  machine's `init.defaultBranch`. Force is on in fixtures because the threat
  is the developer's global excludes file (`core.excludesFile`): a global
  ignore of `.endless/` would silently drop fixture files on one machine only.

## Streamer, Repo and how git runs (Q3, Q4)

- One type. `Repo` holds state plus the optional `dt.StdIO` from RepoArgs.
  `Streamer` is deleted along with the package-level `Commit`,
  `StageModuleFiles` and `UnstageAll` wrappers, which only buffered Streamer's
  output. Mike: streaming is for future callers, not nobody; both benefits in
  one type.
- The rule: operations whose output the package parses (status, rev-parse,
  log, diff) always capture, regardless of StdIO. Operations whose output is
  for a human (commit, add, push, clone, checkout) write to StdIO when set and
  otherwise buffer and return it.
- One run function behind GitRunner, Repo and the creation operations,
  taking ctx, dir, env, stdin, `dt.StdIO` and args; raw `exec.Command`
  disappears from OpenRepo and Streamer. (Fact: today there are three paths,
  GitRunner.runGit in run_git.go buffered with stderr wrapped, OpenRepo in repo.go raw with stderr discarded,
  Streamer.Commit in operations.go raw streaming with no ctx.)

## Go-module knowledge leaves go-gitutil

`StageModuleFiles` finds nested `go.mod` files and stages around them. Mike:
"Go module logic should definitely not be in go-gitutil, but instead in
go-goutil." So:

- `FindNestedModules` moves to go-goutil. gomion's `gommod/goutils` becomes
  go-pkgs/go-goutil, package `goutil`; that extraction is a
  gomion task of its own (the package also holds AST diff, API compatibility,
  dependency analysis).
- go-gitutil keeps the git-only pieces: `UnstageAll`, `StageFileContent`
  (hash-object + update-index), and the new `Add` with `Exclude`.
- gomion composes: `goutil.FindNestedModules`, then `repo.UnstageAll`, then
  `repo.Add(AddArgs{Paths: ["."], Exclude: nested})`.

## Naming

- The package renames from `gitutils` to `gitutil`. Mike: standardize on
  singular `util` across go-pkgs, including renaming go-diffutils. go-diffutils
  is not an Endless project; Mike files that where he tracks it.
- Git domain types (branch name, revision, object id) live in go-dt's root
  package with a `Git` prefix (`GitRefName`, `GitRevision`, `GitObjectID`),
  filed as E-2599 in go-dt. go-gitutil's `GitRef` and `RemoteName` move to
  those types in its implementation task.

## Tests (Q6)

- go-gitutil gets a `test/` module per ED-1650; today it has none and its one
  test, diff_parser_test.go, sits beside the code.
- The test module dogfoods go-fsfix repo fixtures. The build-order friction
  (go-gitutil's tests need a go-fsfix built against the new API) is a tooling
  problem, not an architecture one. Existing tasks: gomion E-2561 (command
  managing go.work across directories) and endless E-1192 (go.work generation
  as a standalone tool).

## The negative test cases (formerly "decoy" files)

gomion's repo_setup_test.go fixture places `go.mod` files at
`dtx/testdata/x/go.mod` and `.endless/worktrees/a/go.mod`, with module paths
literally `ignored/testdata` and `ignored/endless`. They are negative test
cases: gomion's layout classifier must not treat them as modules. They must be
committed because gomion reads tracked files only ("An untracked go.mod is
invisible to CI, so it is invisible here too"), which is why the fixture adds
with Force. "Decoy" was the E-2546 session's word; negative test cases is the
clear one.

## Follow-ups filed

- E-2600 (go-gitutil): Reshape Repo with Init, Clone, Add and Commit. Cleans up
  E-2548; blocks E-2568, E-2559 and E-2556; relates to E-2599. Its analysis
  holds the API shape and the identity/StdIO rules above, as task-level
  decisions.
- E-2602 (go-gitutil): Create go-gitutil's test module on go-fsfix fixtures.
  Blocked by E-2600 and E-2568.
- go-goutil extraction, three parts: Mike created and registered the
  go-goutil project on 2026-11-12; E-2608 (go-goutil) extracts gommod/goutils
  into it as package goutil; E-2601 (gomion) then replaces the local copy with
  the import. E-2608 blocks E-2601.
- E-2607 (gomion, research): Survey go-pkgs for plural util names to rename,
  filing a rename task in each project that needs one (go-diffutils is a
  registered Endless project, so its rename task can be filed there directly).
- Decision ED-1662 (gomion): go-pkgs package names use singular util. Four
  decisions first filed in go-gitutil (ED-1658 to ED-1661) were rejected as
  task-level or misplaced; their content lives in E-2600's analysis and here.
- For Mike: revise E-2556's description. go-gitutil already has Commit,
  UnstageAll and InfoStore, and StageModuleFiles is removed rather than carried
  over, so its remaining work is deleting gomion's copy and switching imports;
  the call-site rewrite is E-2601's.
- E-2609 (endless): rename the `--git-hooks none` choice on project init, which
  installs a plain Git hook rather than nothing.
